description: An information-discovery profile for breast cancer and condition-qualified subtypes. It surfaces public trials, publication metadata and carefully filtered headlines; it does not diagnose, recommend treatment or studies, assess eligibility, or interpret findings.

synopsis.overview: Breast cancer is a group of cancers that begins in breast tissue. It includes different histological and molecular subtypes, and can affect women and men; ductal carcinoma in situ is a non-invasive breast abnormality, while invasive cancers can spread beyond their original site.
synopsis.manifestations: A breast lump or change in breast size or shape, nipple change or discharge, skin dimpling or thickening, or a lump near the armpit can be signs that need clinical assessment. Early breast cancer may have no symptoms, and many breast changes are not cancer.
synopsis.management: Care depends on the cancer's type, stage, grade, receptor and biomarker findings, overall circumstances, and preferences. Treatment may combine surgery, radiotherapy, chemotherapy, endocrine therapy, immunotherapy, targeted therapy, and supportive or reconstructive care; decisions belong with the cancer care team.
synopsis.outlook: The outlook varies substantially by subtype, stage, grade, receptor status, response to treatment, and whether disease has recurred or spread. A general information profile cannot predict an individual's prognosis; current clinical guidance and the treating team provide the appropriate context.

topics.heading: Clinical trials
topics.description: Registered breast-cancer studies, including prevention, screening, diagnosis, treatment, survivorship and metastatic-disease research. A listing does not indicate eligibility or that a study is recommended.

topics.heading: Treatment and care
topics.description: Surgery, radiotherapy, medicines, reconstruction and supportive care used in different breast-cancer settings; treatment choices depend on clinical and pathology findings and require an appropriately qualified care team.

termDefinitions.lumpectomy: Surgery that removes a breast tumour and a margin of surrounding tissue while leaving much of the breast in place; the appropriate operation depends on the clinical situation.
termDefinitions.mastectomy: Surgery to remove breast tissue. The extent and timing of surgery are determined by the cancer, the person and the care team's assessment.
termDefinitions.endocrine therapy: Treatment that blocks or lowers the effect of hormones on cancers whose growth is influenced by hormone receptors.
termDefinitions.targeted therapy: Treatment designed to act on a particular molecular feature or pathway of cancer cells; examples and suitability depend on tumour testing.
termDefinitions.breast reconstruction: Surgery or other reconstruction intended to restore breast shape after breast surgery; it is a personal clinical decision and may be immediate or delayed.

topics.heading: Research
topics.description: Research into breast-cancer biology, prevention, screening, diagnosis, treatment response, recurrence, metastasis, survivorship, disparities and quality of life.

topics.heading: Genetics and tumour biology
topics.description: Inherited risk, tumour biomarkers, receptor status and molecular pathways studied in breast cancer; genetic and pathology results require qualified interpretation rather than self-assessment.

termDefinitions.BRCA1: A gene involved in DNA repair. Inherited pathogenic variants can increase the risk of breast and other cancers, but a gene result requires professional genetic interpretation.
termDefinitions.BRCA2: A gene involved in DNA repair. Inherited pathogenic variants can increase the risk of breast and other cancers, but a gene result requires professional genetic interpretation.
termDefinitions.PALB2: A gene involved in DNA repair whose inherited variants can be associated with increased breast-cancer risk; results require qualified counselling and interpretation.
termDefinitions.HER2: Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2, a protein that can be present at higher levels in some breast cancers and may guide treatment decisions.
termDefinitions.estrogen receptor: A cell protein that can be tested in a breast tumour. Receptor results help clinicians classify disease and consider treatment options.
termDefinitions.progesterone receptor: A cell protein that can be tested in a breast tumour. Receptor results contribute to tumour classification and treatment planning.

topics.heading: Living with breast cancer
topics.description: Life during and after breast-cancer care, including symptoms, treatment effects, work, relationships, body image, fertility, sexuality, follow-up and emotional wellbeing.

topics.heading: Caregiving and support
topics.description: Practical, emotional and communication support for people affected by breast cancer, including family members, care partners, children and people living with advanced disease.

topics.heading: Advocacy and access
topics.description: Patient voice, equitable screening and treatment access, research funding, policy, awareness, inclusion and advocacy for people affected by breast cancer.
